title: Predict before you sweep
brief: Hold lift and dynamic pressure fixed. Predict the change in induced drag when span doubles.
supplied: How does span affect induced drag at fixed lift and condition?

L = 5000 N
pi = 3.141592653589793 (declared parameter)
e = 0.8 dimensionless
q = 240 Pa
b = 10 m
Quasi-steady supplied coefficients. Change only the declared independent quantity; other inputs remain fixed.
This is a bounded teaching calculation. It does not establish aircraft safety, successful takeoff, or behavior outside the specified condition.
Di at b=10 m is about 414.466 N; at b=20 m about 103.617 N.
Check the ratio at twice the span.
Show controls with units, supplied and student results separately, a result trace, and a clear limitation.

Supplied executable experiment recipe:
For each b in [8, 10, 12, 16, 20]:
  configured output = L^2/(pi*e*q*b^2)
  comparison = L^2/(pi*e*q*b^2)
Return the paired values with the declared units.

The app uses the arithmetic evaluator in src/core/onboarding/expression.js. It supports +, -, *, /, ^ and parentheses; it never evaluates an equation as JavaScript.
The reduced induced drag claim excludes structural weight and other design effects.

checks.message: Apply the square of the span ratio.

hints: Hold lift, dynamic pressure and efficiency constant when changing span.
Span appears squared in the denominator of this induced-drag model.
Doubling span gives one quarter of the original induced drag.
